correctness.rationale: The five circuit-hyperplanes intersect pairwise in at most two points, proving that boundaries of five-element sets yield all five standard basis vectors in the oriented excluded-facet module. The long exact sequence gives an integral surjection from \(\bigwedge^4\) of the augmentation lattice, so top integral homology is free of rank 30 and all other reduced integral homology vanishes. Intrinsic incidence blocks and explicit generator relations prove the entire group \(D_4\times D_4\), also exhaustively checked among \(8!\) permutations. The exact character formula is checked element-wise by two independent chain-level computations for all 64 automorphisms; irreducible multiplicities follow by exact inner products. Rational transfer gives the quotient dimensions. The extracted verifier reconstructs boundary ranks and independently checks invariant chain-orbit calculations. Modular checks support but do not replace the integral argument.

value.rationale: The Vámos matroid is a canonical smallest nonrepresentable sparse-paving example, and its automorphism group has two intrinsic commuting dihedral factors distinguished by incidence frequencies of forbidden facets. Their quotient spaces behave differently in rational topology (zero versus one third-cohomology class), an effect invisible in the known Tutte polynomial and rank-30 homology. The exact integral oriented-facet kernel and complete character give reusable symmetry data for this natural object without requiring a broader theorem or integral quotient classification.
